source.text: ወማእከላይሁ፡ ይጐድእ፡ እስከ፡ ሰማይ፡ ከመ፡ መንበረ፡ ለእግዚአብሔር፡ ዘእምእብነ፡ ፔካ፡ ወድማሑ፡ ለመንበረ፡ እምእብነ፡ ሰንፔር።
source.note: New informed author transcription from Charles 1906 printed p.48, unit 8 (primary PDF p.86), personally cross-checked with the original-camera Claremont derivative of the same printed edition. All 13 main-line words were read and lexically/grammatically audited. The disputed token is ወድማሑ, not failed ወደማሑ. Superscript apparatus numbers and the editorial asterisk before እስከ are excluded from the lexical text and described in the explanation. Ethiopic word/final separators are normalized to Unicode. Low confidence is an honest selected-critical-edition scope qualification, not a claim of unknown fidels: no individual fidel or source-word meaning remains unresolved in this proposed row. No manuscript priority, new physical witness for the prior84 copy, or publication approval is claimed.
transcription_uncertainties: Accepted only within the selected Charles 1906 critical main-line scope; the printed editorial asterisk and recorded variants are not manuscript-certified. The low source qualifier is retained without inventing unresolved characters or silently promoting confidence.

translation.text: And its middle[a] juts as far as heaven, like a throne for the Lord made of pēkā-stone.[b] And the top of the throne is of sapphire-stone.[c]

footnotes.text: The source has a middle/central adjective with a third-person singular suffix: literally, its middle. No extra mountain noun or plural their has been inserted. The spatial verb means jut or project here; as far as heaven preserves the stated limit.

Pēkā is the printed stone name. Dillmann’s photographed 1865 Latin entry explicitly cites this verse and describes white marble, perhaps alabaster. The stone name is retained because that does not establish an exact modern mineral identification.

This rendering follows Charles’s 1906 printed critical main line, including its marked editorial wording and the throne in the final clause. Literally the latter has its summit, of/for the throne, from sapphire-stone; the relational construction is rendered the top of the throne is of sapphire-stone. Charles records variants in notes 45–49 and marks the word before heaven with an asterisk. Those variants have not been newly adjudicated against manuscripts. Sapphire is the historical lexical stone name, not a modern gemological certification.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete spatial adjective entry gives medius and cites Hen.18,8; source has a third-person singular suffix. Preserve that suffix rather than silently writing a plural pronoun or adding mountain. Grammar pp.339–341 and 354–357 supplies suffix formation; a one/part sense is implicit in substantival middle, not an added source noun.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete verb entry gives percutere/pulsare and separately trudere, protrudere, explicitly citing Hen.18,8. Here with a spatial limit, jut/project is the bounded spatial sense. Native verb plus Table I u-containing Gamal distinguishes ጐ from ordinary ጎ.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete preposition/conjunction entry includes usque ad and spatial terminus. Source carries a raised asterisk before this word; the star is editorial and is not a fidel.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete entry gives coelum; no plural form is substituted for this printed singular.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Complete entry includes comparative ut, sicut, quemadmodum, quasi. This is a comparison, not a declaration that the formation literally is a divine throne.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Complete entry gives sedes, solium, thronus among senses. Both throne tokens end with the native Rees I shape, not Rees II; the comparative throne sense fits the explicit Lord relation without borrowing an English Enoch text.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Complete divine-name entry explains dominus ... universi and use as the proper name/title of God. The prefix la is kept as for rather than suppressed. Complete la entry covers directional, beneficial and general relational functions.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Complete stone entry gives lapis; final a marks the source construction. Relative za plus em expresses which is of/from. Complete em entry explicitly includes materia, ex qua aliquid fit vel componitur; the relative attaches to the throne phrase, not the Lord.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The actual full entry in col.1392, not merely a head match, explicitly cites Hen.18,8 and gives album marmor, fortasse alabastrites. It notes another cited item differs. The entry ends before the next head; the next photographed page begins the lexicon appendix, not an omitted semantic continuation. Native source Pa/Psa order V matches Table I; pă/pe/pə is not guessed from English. Retain a transparent stone-name rather than assert a modern mineral identity.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Complete photographed entry gives vertex et caput and cites Hen.18,8. Native second fidel has the right extension of Dant VI, not Dant I; actual Yaman VI and same-page Y control differ. Final Haut II retains root consonant plus third-person singular u. Thus reject the preserved failed ወደማሑ reading, not by lexical expectation or model vote.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Read the printed la prefix and Rees I ending, not an assumed u suffix. La can introduce the relational noun after a preceding suffixed noun; complete la entry describes its general relation and use with anticipatory suffixes. The source literally retains summit/its plus la-throne; top of the throne renders that relation without changing throne to mountain.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The second stone construction repeats em plus stone, with an English copula supplied for the nominal predicate. Do not invent an additional source verb or qualitative modifier.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Dillmann 1865, actual complete photographed Latin entry; 1907 grammar where stated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The complete actual entry in col.375 gives sapphirus and explicitly cites Hen.18,8. The name is represented as sapphire in its historical lexical sense, without certifying a modern gemological identification.
